messages:
sanjay: quick follow-up from the RFC sync — re: pacing + budget windows for rate-limiting. TL;DR: proposal to add client-level "budget buckets" (daily + rolling minute) + dynamic pacing tokens to smooth bursts, and a small graceful-fallback path for suspected abuse.

amy: can you paste the concrete config example? want to see how this wires into ingress.

sanjay: sure — example we discussed:
``
quota_policy:
  - scope: client_id
    daily_budget: 1_000_000
    rolling_minute: 5_000
    pacing:
      token_rate: 200/s
      burst: 1_000
      grace_tokens: 200
```
This is enforced at the edge; pacing tokens are returned in headers so SDKs can backoff.

leo: two quick things:
- where does fairness scheduler fit? per-customer budgets + global fairness layer that peeks at live latency/queue depth
- how do we handle long-lived streaming sessions (they can exhaust rolling_minute unfairly)

marcus: for streaming we should switch to an active session lease model: lease tokens reserved from the rolling window at session start, periodically renewed. prevents small interactive sessions from being starved.

diane: about abuse detection — are we coupling heuristics into the quota decision path? I worry about latency overhead if we call classification inline.

sanjay: good call. proposal: keep heuristics asynchronous for most cases (score persisted to redis/feature-store) and only apply hard-deny on high-confidence signals. Inline checks limited to a very cheap rule-set (rate-of-new-user-keys, malformed prompts, obvious credential stuffing patterns).

amy: does that mean we return 429s only for pacing/budget violations and 403/410 for confirmed abuse? we need clear signals for client teams.

sanjay: yes. policy:
- soft: 429 Retry-After header + X-Rate-Paced: true (client should backoff)
- grace: allow limited excess (grace_tokens) and emit X-Grace-Used
- hard: 403 + audit log entry when abuse confirmed

ops-bot: reminder: any change to 429 semantics must be communicated to SDKs and gateways. created ticket #3472.

leo: how do we measure fairness? we had earlier a fairness score — want to avoid global starvation if a few high-QPS clients hog the batched GPUs.

marcus: fairness metric we liked: median-latency uplift per customer over baseline and percent of denied requests. scheduler tries to equalize 95th pct latency delta under config knobs.

diane: operational question — where do we keep budget state? redis? cockroach? we need cross-region view for global routing.

sanjay: implementation plan:
- hot-path state in sharded in-memory store in the edge cluster (fast check)
- durable counters in cockroach + periodic sync for long-term budgets (daily resets, audits)
- use vector-clock-ish leases to avoid races in multi-edge writes

amy: what's the plan for rollout? canary + progressive enable by client tier?

sanjay: yes. rollout plan:
1) opt-in beta for dev accounts — pacing only (no hard denies)
2) enable grace_tokens enforcement for standard tier
3) enterprise-only hard-denies and regional/global quotas
4) full enable with abuser-auto-block after monitoring window

leo: any impact on continuous batching? token pacing could reduce batch efficiency if tokens are too strict.

marcus: we should expose a batching hint to the scheduler: allow small delay (max 20ms) to coalesce into bigger batches when request rate is near batch sweet-spot. Config knob: batching_margin_ms.

diane: security note: audit logs must include effective policy id and feature flags used to decide each deny — for compliance.

sanjay: agreed. also: put an immutable policy id header on responses: X-Quota-Policy: qpol_2026_03_v1. That will make posthoc analysis straightforward.

amy: testing matrix: we need synthetic workloads:
- many low-qps clients vs few high-qps clients
- mixed streaming + short requests
- simulated abuser (credential stuffing + high token churn)

sanjay: created a test harness ticket and added sample scripts.

leo: last thing — we should avoid embedding heuristics in SDKs. SDK should surface headers and expose a backoff utility, but not try to decide abuse locally.

marcus: Agreed. SDKs = reactive, server = authoritative.

diane: ok. next steps? I can take a pass at the rollout playbook (alerts, dashboards, runbooks).

sanjay: please do. i'll update the RFC with the config examples and we can review tomorrow. @kai fyi — want your eyes on the lease protocol.

kai: looking now. small nit: for lease renewals, add jitter to avoid thundering herd. also suggest exponential backoff for SDK retries when 429 persisted.

sanjay: good call. adding jitter + backoff guidance to the doc.

ops-bot: deploy-check: policy-id qpol_2026_03_v1 validated in staging, no regressions found. :white_check_mark:

amy: thanks — moving this to action items in the RFC thread. will ping infra for the cockroach schema.

marcus: thumbs up. :+1:

sanjay: closing loop for now. will post updated RFC link in the morning.
